title: Elodie and the Garden
premise: Coral Underhill, a mercenary sworn to a silent god, has never left the valley where magic cannot follow—until he discovers tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies and is pulled into its pages. The prophecy demands he steal back a soul sold to the court beneath the mountain: the soul of Elodie, a gardener who once tended his family's land and traded herself to save the valley. As Coral descends through thirteen turning moons, he learns his god's silence and Elodie's bargain are the same wound—the court beneath feeds on oaths, and his loyalty was inherited from a lie. In the climax he breaks his oath publicly, trading his own remembered name for Elodie's soul; they return to a valley where magic now seeps in gently, and Coral, nameless but free, plants her garden anew.
about_author: Freya Oyelaran is a former botanist who writes fantasy rooted in soil, seasons, and the debts families pass down like heirlooms. She lives at the edge of a real valley and insists the prophecies there are better behaved.

chapters.title: The Date Written in Water
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the godless valley, Coral tends mercenary work and an inherited shrine, until a scholar shows him his own date inked in a prophecy book older than his grandmother. That night the words pull him bodily from the valley into the world of magic. Emotional beat: dread braided with a strange relief—he was always meant to leave.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns Beneath
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with interludes from Elodie's memories surfacing in the mountain's halls. Descending toward the court, Coral learns the soul he must steal belongs to Elodie, who saved the valley by selling herself—and that his god went silent paying her price. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling as he realizes his inheritance is a debt disguised as faith.

chapters.title: What the Court Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Coral and Elodie, who remembers everything and has made peace she shouldn't have. Coral reaches the throne of oaths on the twelfth moon's turn; the court offers him his god's voice back if he leaves Elodie. He refuses, shattering his sworn blade before the throne. Emotional beat: the climax—truth chosen over loyalty, at terrible cost.

chapters.title: A Garden Without Prophecy
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, then shared. Freed but stripped of Coral's name, the two walk home to a valley where magic now enters like spring water. Elodie replants her garden; Coral, nameless, chooses a new one from her seed catalog. The god speaks once—a thank-you, nothing more. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; inheritance remade as choice rather than debt.
